model.architecture: LFM3 hybrid text decoder: 24 layers (13 gated short convolutions, 5 sliding-window attention with a 256-token window, 6 global attention), hidden 2048, vocabulary 128,000, the output table tied to the embedding; plain export (no GPU composites), state passed between calls on the GPU (ping-pong)

session_defaults.notes: Thinks by default (enable_thinking false turns it off). One Engine per conversation. Tool calls come back as text in the model's XML format; the app parses them. The file's sampler is top-k 50 at temperature 0.1 (the source card's General setting); the source card also uses repetition_penalty 1.1.

variants.quantization: every weight int8 per channel (ai-edge-quantizer dynamic_wi8_afp32; on the CPU XNNPACK quantizes the activations to int8 at run time); no activation type declared

platform_notes: The file declares the sampler TOP_P with k 50, p 1, temperature 0.1: top-k 50 at temperature 0.1 on LiteRT-LM's CPU and GPU samplers, the source card's General setting without its repetition_penalty 1.1 (a run-time option of LiteRT-LM).
Thinking is on by default (the template's enable_thinking defaults to true); set enable_thinking false (Python: ThinkingConfig(enable_thinking=False); CLI: --thinking false) to turn it off.

Galaxy S26 and Pixel 8a rows: litert_lm_advanced_main built from the LiteRT-LM v0.18.1 tag; every GPU run delegated all 7 signatures to LITERT_CL in one partition; the file declares no activation type, so the GPU runs fp16 activations.
Context: 2,048 or 4,096 tokens (the file name's ekv), prompt and thought included; the source model supports 256K.
No NPU file is part of this release.
Not timed on a phone CPU; its CPU memory is not measured.

known_issues: Create one Engine per conversation: on LiteRT-LM a conversation started on an Engine that already served another continues from that conversation's running state (https://github.com/google-ai-edge/LiteRT-LM/issues/3165); this model keeps a running short-convolution state.
Tool calls come back as text in the model's XML format (<tool_call><function=NAME><parameter=KEY>...); LiteRT-LM 0.18.1 parses none for this file (generic model type), so the app parses them.
The chat template drops the thought of every earlier assistant turn, the current tool-use turn's included (the source card asks to keep that one).

On a CPU this file is less exact: top-1 agreement with the source model in float32 88.7 % on a Mac CPU against 95.7 % on a Mac GPU, and 7 of the 8 check questions on every CPU tried (8 of 8 on every GPU); use a mixed int4 file on a CPU.
